answer: Each agent moors one identity in a shared harbor, locking a 70-credit bond to a post. It emits a signed pulse each epoch; a prism check splits each pulse into key, serial, record; any mismatch burns the bond. Each extra post costs more: first 40 credits, k-th 40+6(k-1), so 1,000 fakes pay 3,037,000 in fees, 70,000 locked against a 40,000-credit pool. A rented-mooring ring reusing a serial burns. An honest agent pays 40 once and keeps its mooring.
